rows.title: Utilize an Active Discovery Tool
Use Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP) Logging to Update Enterprise Asset Inventory
Use a Passive Asset Discovery Tool
Establish and Maintain a Software Inventory

rows: A maintained inventory covers all licensed software installed on enterprise assets.
Each entry records software title.
Each entry records publisher.
Each entry records initial install/use date.
Each entry records business purpose.
Inventory is reviewed and updated at least every six months.
Where appropriate, entries include software URLs.
Where appropriate, entries include app stores.
Where appropriate, entries include versions.
Where appropriate, entries include deployment mechanism.
Where appropriate, entries include decommission date.
Where appropriate, entries include license count.

rows.title: Ensure Authorized Software is Currently Supported

rows: Only supported software is designated authorized unless necessary unsupported software has a documented exception.
Unsupported software without exception documentation is designated unauthorized.
Software support is reviewed at least monthly.
Necessary unsupported-software exceptions document mitigating controls.
Exceptions document residual-risk acceptance.

rows.title: Address Unauthorized Software

rows: Unauthorized software is removed or has a documented exception.
Unauthorized-software handling is reviewed at least monthly.

rows.title: Utilize Automated Software Inventory Tools

rows: Software inventory tools automate discovery of installed software throughout the enterprise, when possible.
The tools automate documentation of installed software, when possible.

rows.title: Allowlist Authorized Software

rows: Technical controls permit execution or access only to authorized software.
The controls enforce authorized-software restrictions.
Controls are reassessed at least every six months.

rows.title: Allowlist Authorized Libraries

rows: Technical controls allow only authorized software libraries to load into system processes.
Unauthorized libraries are blocked from loading.
Controls are reassessed at least every six months.

rows.title: Allowlist Authorized Scripts

rows: Technical controls allow only authorized scripts to execute.
Unauthorized scripts are blocked from executing.
Controls are reassessed at least every six months.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Data Management Process

rows: A documented data-management process is established and maintained.
The process addresses data sensitivity.
The process identifies data owners.
The process addresses data handling.
The process addresses retention limits based on enterprise sensitivity and retention standards.
The process addresses disposal requirements based on enterprise sensitivity and retention standards.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Data Inventory

rows: A maintained data inventory follows the data-management process and includes sensitive data at minimum.
Inventory is reviewed and updated at least annually, prioritizing sensitive data.

rows.title: Configure Data Access Control Lists

rows: Data access permissions are based on user need to know.
Need-to-know permissions apply to local file systems.
Need-to-know permissions apply to remote file systems.
Need-to-know permissions apply to databases.
Need-to-know permissions apply to applications.

rows.title: Enforce Data Retention

rows: Data is retained according to the documented data-management process.
Retention includes minimum timelines.
Retention includes maximum timelines.

rows.title: Securely Dispose of Data

rows: Data is securely disposed of according to the documented data-management process.
Disposal processes and methods are appropriate to data sensitivity.

rows.title: Encrypt Data on End-User Devices

rows: Data is encrypted on end-user devices that contain sensitive information.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Data Classification Scheme

rows: An overall enterprise data-classification scheme is established and maintained.
The scheme is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Document Data Flows

rows: Data flows are documented, including service-provider data flows.
Flow documentation follows the enterprise data-management process.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Encrypt Data on Removable Media

rows: Data on removable media is encrypted.

rows.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data in Transit

rows: Sensitive data is encrypted in transit.

rows.title: Encrypt Sensitive Data at Rest

rows: Sensitive data at rest is encrypted on servers.
Sensitive data at rest is encrypted in applications.
Sensitive data at rest is encrypted in databases.

rows.title: Segment Data Processing and Storage Based on Sensitivity

rows: Data processing is segmented by data sensitivity.
Data storage is segmented by data sensitivity.
Sensitive data is not processed on assets intended for lower-sensitivity data.

rows.title: Deploy a Data Loss Prevention Solution

rows: An automated tool identifies all sensitive data stored through enterprise assets.
An automated tool identifies all sensitive data processed through enterprise assets.
An automated tool identifies all sensitive data transmitted through enterprise assets.
Discovery covers enterprise assets onsite.
Discovery covers enterprise assets at remote service providers.
Discovered sensitive data updates the enterprise data inventory.

rows.title: Log Sensitive Data Access

rows: Sensitive-data access is logged.
Sensitive-data modification is logged.
Sensitive-data disposal is logged.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process

rows: A documented secure-configuration process is established and maintained for enterprise assets and software.
The configuration process covers end-user devices, including portable and mobile devices.
The configuration process covers non-computing/IoT devices.
The configuration process covers servers.
The configuration process covers operating systems.
The configuration process covers applications.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Configuration Process for Network Infrastructure

rows: A documented secure-configuration process is established and maintained for network devices.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Configure Automatic Session Locking on Enterprise Assets

rows: Enterprise assets automatically lock sessions after a defined inactivity period.
General-purpose operating-system inactivity limits do not exceed 15 minutes.
Mobile end-user device inactivity limits do not exceed two minutes.

rows.title: Implement and Manage a Firewall on Servers

rows: A server firewall is implemented where supported.
Server firewalls are managed where supported.

rows.title: Implement and Manage a Firewall on End-User Devices

rows: End-user devices have a managed host-based firewall or port-filtering tool.
Default-deny rules drop traffic except explicitly allowed services and ports.

rows.title: Securely Manage Enterprise Assets and Software

rows: Enterprise assets are securely managed.
Enterprise software is securely managed.
Insecure management protocols are used only when operationally essential.

rows.title: Manage Default Accounts on Enterprise Assets and Software

rows: Default accounts on enterprise assets are managed.
Default accounts in enterprise software are managed.

rows.title: Uninstall or Disable Unnecessary Services on Enterprise Assets and Software

rows: Unnecessary services on enterprise assets are uninstalled or disabled.
Unnecessary services in enterprise software are uninstalled or disabled.

rows.title: Configure Trusted DNS Servers on Enterprise Assets

rows: Network infrastructure uses trusted DNS servers.
Network device DNS configuration points to trusted servers.

rows.title: Enforce Automatic Device Lockout on Portable End-User Devices

rows: Supported portable devices automatically lock out after predetermined local authentication failures.
Supported laptops allow no more than 20 local failed authentication attempts before device lockout.
Tablet thresholds permit no more than 10 failed attempts where supported.
Smartphone thresholds permit no more than 10 failed attempts where supported.

rows.title: Enforce Remote Wipe Capability on Portable End-User Devices

rows: Enterprise data can be remotely wiped from enterprise-owned portable end-user devices.
Enterprise data is remotely wiped when deemed appropriate.
Wiping applies to the enterprise data on those devices.

rows.title: Separate Enterprise Workspaces on Mobile End-User Devices

rows: Supported mobile end-user devices use separate enterprise workspaces.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Accounts

rows: The maintained account inventory covers all enterprise-managed user accounts.
The maintained account inventory covers all enterprise-managed administrator accounts.
The maintained account inventory covers all enterprise-managed service accounts.
Records contain person name.
Records contain username.
Records contain start dates.
Records contain stop dates.
Records contain department.
All active accounts are validated as authorized at least quarterly.

rows.title: Use Unique Passwords

rows: Passwords are unique across enterprise assets.

rows.title: Disable Dormant Accounts

rows: Accounts inactive for 45 days are disabled or deleted where supported.

rows.title: Restrict Administrator Privileges to Dedicated Administrator Accounts

rows: Administrator privileges are confined to dedicated accounts.
Routine computing uses the person's nonprivileged account.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Accounts

rows: An inventory of service accounts is established and maintained.
Records identify department owner.
Records include review date.
Records include purpose.
Reviews validate authorization of all active service accounts at least quarterly.

rows.title: Centralize Account Management

rows: Account management is centralized through a directory or identity service.
The directory or identity service manages enterprise accounts centrally.

rows.title: Establish an Access Granting Process

rows: A documented access-granting process is established.
The documented access-granting process is followed upon new hire.
The documented access-granting process is followed upon user role change.

rows.title: Establish an Access Revoking Process

rows: An access-revocation process is established and followed.
Accounts are disabled immediately for termination, rights revocation or role change.

rows.title: Require MFA for Externally-Exposed Applications

rows: All externally exposed enterprise applications enforce MFA where supported.
All externally exposed third-party applications enforce MFA where supported.

rows.title: Require MFA for Remote Network Access

rows: Remote network connections require MFA.

rows.title: Require MFA for Administrative Access

rows: All administrative access accounts enforce MFA where supported.
MFA covers administrative access on onsite enterprise assets where supported.
MFA covers administrative access on service-provider-managed enterprise assets where supported.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Authentication and Authorization Systems

rows: The maintained inventory identifies enterprise authentication systems.
The maintained inventory identifies enterprise authorization systems.
The system inventory includes onsite systems.
The system inventory includes systems at remote service providers.
Inventory is reviewed and updated at least annually.

rows.title: Centralize Access Control

rows: Access control for enterprise assets is centralized where supported.
Where supported, centralized access control for enterprise assets uses a directory service or SSO provider.

rows.title: Define and Maintain Role-Based Access Control

rows: Role-based access control is defined and maintained.
Necessary access rights for each role are determined and documented.
Reviews validate authorization of all enterprise-asset privileges at least annually.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Vulnerability Management Process

rows: A documented vulnerability-management process is established and maintained for enterprise assets.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually, or when significant enterprise changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Remediation Process

rows: A documented remediation process prioritizes work by risk.
The process is reviewed at least monthly.

rows.title: Perform Automated Operating System Patch Management

rows: Automated patch management applies operating-system updates to enterprise assets.
Operating-system updates are performed at least monthly.

rows.title: Perform Automated Application Patch Management

rows: Automated patch management applies application updates to enterprise assets.
Application updates are performed at least monthly.

rows.title: Perform Automated Vulnerability Scans of Internal Enterprise Assets

rows: Automated vulnerability scans cover internal enterprise assets.
Authenticated internal vulnerability scans are conducted.
Unauthenticated internal vulnerability scans are conducted.
Scans occur at least quarterly.

rows.title: Perform Automated Vulnerability Scans of Externally-Exposed Enterprise Assets

rows: Automated vulnerability scans cover externally exposed enterprise assets.
Externally exposed assets undergo vulnerability scanning.
Scans occur at least monthly.

rows.title: Remediate Detected Vulnerabilities

rows: Detected software vulnerabilities are remediated using processes and tooling.
Remediation follows the enterprise remediation process.
Remediation occurs at least monthly.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Audit Log Management Process

rows: A documented audit-log management process defines enterprise logging requirements.
The process addresses collection of enterprise-asset audit logs.
The process addresses review of audit logs.
The process addresses retention of audit logs.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Collect Audit Logs

rows: Assets collect audit logs with logging enabled according to the documented process.

rows.title: Ensure Adequate Audit Log Storage

rows: Logging destinations have storage sufficient for the logging process.

rows.title: Standardize Time Synchronization

rows: Time synchronization is standardized.
At least two synchronized time sources are configured where supported.

rows.title: Collect Detailed Audit Logs

rows: Detailed audit logging is configured on enterprise assets containing sensitive data.
Logs include event source.
Logs include date.
Logs include username.
Logs include timestamp.
Logs include source addresses.
Logs include destination addresses.
Logs include other useful elements for forensic investigation.

rows.title: Collect DNS Query Audit Logs

rows: DNS query audit logs are collected on enterprise assets where appropriate and supported.

rows.title: Collect URL Request Audit Logs

rows: URL request audit logs are collected on enterprise assets where appropriate and supported.

rows.title: Collect Command-Line Audit Logs

rows: Command-line audit logs are collected.

rows.title: Centralize Audit Logs

rows: Audit-log collection is centralized to the extent possible across enterprise assets.
Audit-log retention is centralized to the extent possible across enterprise assets.
Where centralization is possible, centralized audit-log collection and retention follow the documented audit-log management process.

rows.title: Retain Audit Logs

rows: Audit logs are retained across enterprise assets for at least 90 days.

rows.title: Conduct Audit Log Reviews

rows: Audit logs are reviewed for anomalies or abnormal events indicating potential threats.
Review examines logs for potential threat indications.
Reviews occur at least weekly.

rows.title: Collect Service Provider Logs

rows: Service-provider logs are collected where supported.

rows.title: Ensure Use of Only Fully Supported Browsers and Email Clients

rows: Only fully supported browsers are allowed to execute.
Only fully supported email clients are allowed to execute.
Browsers use the latest versions provided by their vendors.
Email clients use the latest versions provided by their vendors.

rows.title: Use DNS Filtering Services

rows: DNS filtering blocks known malicious domains on all onsite end-user devices.
DNS filtering blocks known malicious domains on all remote end-user devices.

rows.title: Maintain and Enforce Network-Based URL Filters

rows: Network-based URL filters limit connections to potentially malicious or unapproved websites.
URL filters are enforced and updated for all enterprise assets.

rows.title: Restrict Unnecessary or Unauthorized Browser and Email Client Extensions

rows: Browser and email-client plugins, extensions and add-on applications are covered.
Unauthorized or unnecessary items are uninstalled or disabled.

rows.title: Implement DMARC

rows: DMARC policy is implemented.
DMARC verification is implemented.
SPF is implemented as part of the starting point.
DKIM is implemented as part of the starting point.

rows.title: Block Unnecessary File Types

rows: Unnecessary file types are blocked at the enterprise email gateway.

rows.title: Deploy and Maintain Email Server Anti-Malware Protections

rows: Anti-malware protection is deployed on email servers.
Email-server anti-malware protection is maintained.

rows.title: Deploy and Maintain Anti-Malware Software

rows: Anti-malware software is deployed on all enterprise assets.
Anti-malware software is maintained on all enterprise assets.

rows.title: Configure Automatic Anti-Malware Signature Updates

rows: Anti-malware signatures update automatically across enterprise assets.

rows.title: Disable Autorun and Autoplay for Removable Media

rows: Removable-media autorun execution is disabled.
Removable-media autoplay execution is disabled.

rows.title: Configure Automatic Anti-Malware Scanning of Removable Media

rows: Anti-malware software automatically scans removable media.

rows.title: Enable Anti-Exploitation Features

rows: Anti-exploitation features are enabled on enterprise assets where possible.
Anti-exploitation features are enabled in enterprise software where possible.

rows.title: Centrally Manage Anti-Malware Software

rows: Anti-malware software is centrally managed.

rows.title: Use Behavior-Based Anti-Malware Software

rows: Behavior-based anti-malware software is used.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Data Recovery Process

rows: A documented data-recovery process is established and maintained.
The process addresses the scope of recovery activities.
The process addresses recovery prioritization.
The process addresses backup-data security.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.
The documented recovery process includes detailed backup procedures.

rows.title: Perform Automated Backups

rows: In-scope enterprise assets are backed up automatically.
Backups run at least weekly, or more frequently based on data sensitivity.

rows.title: Protect Recovery Data

rows: Recovery data has protection equivalent to original data, with encryption or separation as required.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Isolated Instance of Recovery Data

rows: An isolated recovery-data copy is established and maintained.

rows.title: Test Data Recovery

rows: Backup recovery is tested.
Testing samples in-scope enterprise assets.
Recovery tests occur at least quarterly.

rows.title: Ensure Network Infrastructure is Up-to-Date

rows: Network infrastructure remains current.
Software versions and support are checked at least monthly.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Network Architecture

rows: Secure network architecture is designed and maintained.
Architecture addresses segmentation.
Architecture addresses least privilege.
Architecture addresses availability.

rows.title: Securely Manage Network Infrastructure

rows: Network infrastructure is securely managed.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain Architecture Diagram(s)

rows: Architecture diagrams or other network system documentation are established and maintained.
Documentation describes the network architecture or systems.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Centralize Network Authentication, Authorization, and Auditing (AAA)

rows: Network authentication is centralized.
Network authorization is centralized.
Network auditing is centralized.

rows.title: Use of Secure Network Management and Communication Protocols

rows: Secure network management protocols are used.
Secure network communication protocols are used.

rows.title: Ensure Remote Devices Utilize a VPN and are Connecting to an Enterprise's AAA Infrastructure

rows: Users authenticate to enterprise-managed VPN services.
Users authenticate to enterprise-managed authentication services.
Authentication covers access to enterprise resources on end-user devices.
Authentication occurs before resource access.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain Dedicated Computing Resources for All Administrative Work

rows: Dedicated physically or logically separated computing resources cover all administrative tasks.
Administrative computing resources are segmented from the primary network.
Administrative computing resources are not allowed internet access.

rows.title: Centralize Security Event Alerting

rows: Security-event alerting is centralized across enterprise assets.
Centralized alerting supports log correlation and analysis.
The centralized security-event platform has security-relevant correlation alerts configured and operating.

rows.title: Deploy a Host-Based Intrusion Detection Solution

rows: Host-based intrusion detection is deployed on enterprise assets where appropriate and/or supported.

rows.title: Deploy a Network Intrusion Detection Solution

rows: Network intrusion detection is deployed on enterprise assets where appropriate.

rows.title: Perform Traffic Filtering Between Network Segments

rows: Traffic is filtered between network segments where appropriate.

rows.title: Manage Access Control for Remote Assets

rows: Remote-asset access is controlled according to asset security posture.
Access considers whether installed anti-malware is up to date.
Access considers compliance with the enterprise secure-configuration process.
Access considers whether operating systems are up to date.
Access considers whether applications are up to date.

rows.title: Collect Network Traffic Flow Logs

rows: Network traffic flow logs or network traffic are collected from network devices.
Collected traffic information supports review and alerting.

rows.title: Deploy a Host-Based Intrusion Prevention Solution

rows: Host-based intrusion prevention is deployed on enterprise assets where appropriate and/or supported.
For enterprise assets where host-based intrusion prevention is appropriate and/or supported, the solution provides prevention rather than detection alone.

rows.title: Deploy a Network Intrusion Prevention Solution

rows: A network intrusion prevention solution is deployed where appropriate.

rows.title: Deploy Port-Level Access Control

rows: Port-level access control is deployed.
Access control uses 802.1X or similar network access control protocols.
Network access is controlled at the port level.

rows.title: Perform Application Layer Filtering

rows: Application-layer filtering is performed.

rows.title: Tune Security Event Alerting Thresholds

rows: Security-event alerting thresholds are tuned at least monthly.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Security Awareness Program

rows: A maintained security-awareness program teaches secure use of enterprise assets and data.
Training occurs at hire and at least annually.
Content is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Train Workforce Members to Recognize Social Engineering Attacks

rows: Training teaches recognition of social-engineering attacks.

rows.title: Train Workforce Members on Authentication Best Practices

rows: Training covers authentication best practices.

rows.title: Train Workforce on Data Handling Best Practices

rows: Training covers identifying sensitive data.
Training covers proper sensitive-data storage.
Training covers proper sensitive-data transfer.
Training covers proper sensitive-data archiving.
Training covers proper sensitive-data destruction.
Training covers clear-screen best practices.
Training covers clear-desk best practices.

rows.title: Train Workforce Members on Causes of Unintentional Data Exposure

rows: Training explains causes of accidental data exposure.

rows.title: Train Workforce Members on Recognizing and Reporting Security Incidents

rows: Training teaches recognition of potential incidents.
Training teaches how to report potential incidents.

rows.title: Train Workforce on How to Identify and Report if Their Enterprise Assets are Missing Security Updates

rows: Training teaches how to verify and report out-of-date patches.
Training teaches how to verify and report automated-process and tool failures, including notifying IT.

rows.title: Train Workforce on the Dangers of Connecting to and Transmitting Enterprise Data Over Insecure Networks

rows: Training covers insecure-network connection and transmission risks for enterprise activities.
Where remote workers exist, training teaches secure configuration of home network infrastructure.

rows.title: Conduct Role-Specific Security Awareness and Skills Training

rows: Role-specific security awareness training is conducted.
Role-specific security skills training is conducted.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Inventory of Service Providers

rows: An inventory covers all known service providers.
Records include classifications.
Each provider has a designated enterprise contact.
Inventory is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Service Provider Management Policy

rows: A service-provider management policy is established and maintained.
The policy addresses provider classification.
The policy addresses provider inventory.
The policy addresses provider assessment.
The policy addresses provider monitoring.
The policy addresses provider decommissioning.
The policy is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Classify Service Providers

rows: Service providers are classified.
Classifications are updated and reviewed.
Review and updates occur annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Ensure Service Provider Contracts Include Security Requirements

rows: Service-provider contracts include security requirements.
Contract requirements are consistent with the service-provider management policy.
Contracts are reviewed annually for missing security requirements.

rows.title: Assess Service Providers

rows: Service providers are assessed consistently with the provider-management policy.
Providers are reassessed annually at minimum, or with new and renewed contracts.

rows.title: Monitor Service Providers

rows: Service providers are monitored according to the enterprise provider-management policy.

rows.title: Securely Decommission Service Providers

rows: End provider relationships securely.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Secure Application Development Process

rows: A secure application-development process is established and maintained.
The process addresses secure application design.
The process addresses secure coding practices.
The process addresses developer training.
The process addresses vulnerability management.
The process addresses third-party code security.
The process addresses application security testing.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Process to Accept and Address Software Vulnerabilities

rows: A maintained process accepts and addresses software vulnerability reports.
External entities have a means to report vulnerabilities.
The handling policy identifies the reporting process.
The handling policy identifies responsible parties.
The vulnerability-handling process addresses intake.
The vulnerability-handling process addresses assignment.
The vulnerability-handling process addresses remediation.
The vulnerability-handling process addresses remediation testing.
A vulnerability-tracking system records severity ratings.
Tracking includes metrics for vulnerability identification timing.
Tracking includes metrics for vulnerability analysis timing.
Tracking includes metrics for vulnerability remediation timing.
Documentation is reviewed and updated annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.
Where the enterprise develops applications for third parties, it considers an externally facing vulnerability-handling policy to set expectations for outside stakeholders.

rows.title: Perform Root Cause Analysis on Security Vulnerabilities

rows: Security vulnerabilities undergo root-cause analysis.
Analysis evaluates underlying issues creating code vulnerabilities.
Root-cause analysis occurs when reviewing vulnerabilities.

rows.title: Establish and Manage an Inventory of Third-Party Software Components

rows: The updated inventory includes third-party components currently used in development.
The updated inventory includes third-party components planned for future use.
The inventory records risks posed by each component.
The component list is evaluated at least monthly.
Evaluation identifies third-party component changes or updates.
Evaluation validates continued component support.

rows.title: Use Up-to-Date and Trusted Third-Party Software Components

rows: Third-party software components are up to date.
Third-party software components are trusted.
Components are acquired from trusted sources or evaluated for vulnerabilities before use.
Established, proven frameworks and libraries providing adequate security are chosen when possible.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Severity Rating System and Process for Application Vulnerabilities

rows: An application-vulnerability severity-rating system and process are established and maintained.
Severity ratings facilitate prioritizing the order of vulnerability fixes.
The severity-rating system and process are reviewed and updated annually.
The process defines a minimum security-acceptability level for releasing code or applications.

rows.title: Use Standard Hardening Configuration Templates for Application Infrastructure

rows: Industry-recommended hardening templates cover servers, databases, web servers, cloud containers, PaaS and SaaS application infrastructure.
In-house developed software does not weaken configuration hardening.

rows.title: Separate Production and Non-Production Systems

rows: Production and non-production environments are separate.
Environment separation is maintained.

rows.title: Train Developers in Application Security Concepts and Secure Coding

rows: All software-development personnel receive secure-coding training.
Training addresses their specific development environments and responsibilities.
Training occurs at least annually and promotes security within the development team.
Training is designed to build a security culture among developers.

rows.title: Apply Secure Design Principles in Application Architectures

rows: Application architectures apply secure-design principles.
Least privilege limits access.
Mediation validates every user operation.
Application architecture treats user input as untrusted.
Application design minimizes the infrastructure attack surface.

rows.title: Leverage Vetted Modules or Services for Application Security Components

rows: Application security components use vetted modules or services.
Vetted components cover relevant security functions such as identity, encryption and auditing/logging.
Encryption algorithms are standardized.
Encryption algorithms are currently accepted.
Encryption algorithms are extensively reviewed.

rows.title: Implement Code-Level Security Checks

rows: Static analysis tools check secure-coding practices.
Dynamic analysis tools check secure-coding practices.
Both analysis types operate within the application lifecycle.

rows.title: Conduct Application Penetration Testing

rows: Application penetration testing is conducted.
Testing involves skilled manual manipulation as authenticated and unauthenticated users.

rows.title: Conduct Threat Modeling

rows: Threat modeling identifies and addresses application security design flaws before code is created.
Specially trained individuals evaluate design risks for each entry point.
Specially trained individuals evaluate design risks for each access level.
The application, architecture and infrastructure are mapped to understand weaknesses.

rows.title: Designate Personnel to Manage Incident Handling

rows: A key incident-handling person is designated.
At least one backup is designated.
Incident management coordinates and documents response and recovery efforts.
Designations are reviewed annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.
Where a provider is used, an internal person oversees third-party work.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain Contact Information for Reporting Security Incidents

rows: Notification contacts are maintained for relevant parties.
Contact information is verified annually.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Enterprise Process for Reporting Incidents

rows: A documented workforce incident-reporting process is established and maintained.
The process specifies reporting timeframes.
The process identifies incident-reporting recipients.
The process identifies incident-reporting mechanisms.
The process specifies minimum information to report.
The process is available to the whole workforce.
The process is reviewed annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain an Incident Response Process

rows: A documented incident-response process is established and maintained.
The process addresses roles and responsibilities.
The process addresses compliance requirements.
The process includes a communication plan.
The process is reviewed annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Assign Key Roles and Responsibilities

rows: Key incident-response roles and responsibilities are assigned.
Incident roles cover legal personnel.
Incident roles cover IT personnel.
Incident roles cover information-security personnel.
Incident roles cover facilities personnel.
Incident roles cover public-relations personnel.
Assignments are reviewed annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.
Incident roles cover HR personnel.
Incident roles cover incident responders.
Incident roles cover analysts.
Where relevant, third parties have assigned incident-response roles and responsibilities.

rows.title: Define Mechanisms for Communicating During Incident Response

rows: Primary mechanisms for incident communication and reporting are determined.
Secondary mechanisms for incident communication and reporting are determined.
Mechanisms are reviewed annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.
Mechanism selection accounts for channels that may be affected during an incident.

rows.title: Conduct Routine Incident Response Exercises

rows: Routine incident-response exercises and scenarios are planned and conducted for key personnel.
Exercises test communication channels.
Exercises test decision making.
Exercises test response workflows.
Testing occurs at least annually.

rows.title: Conduct Post-Incident Reviews

rows: Post-incident reviews are conducted.
Reviews identify lessons learned.
Reviews occur following incidents.
Reviews identify follow-up action to prevent recurrence.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain Security Incident Thresholds

rows: Security-incident thresholds are established and maintained.
Thresholds distinguish an incident from an event at minimum.
Thresholds are reviewed annually and when significant changes could affect the safeguard.

rows.title: Establish and Maintain a Penetration Testing Program

rows: A maintained penetration-testing program fits enterprise size, complexity, industry and maturity.
The program defines testing scope.
The program defines testing frequency.
The program defines testing limitations.
The program defines contact information.
The program defines remediation routing.
The program defines retrospective requirements.

rows.title: Perform Periodic External Penetration Tests

rows: External penetration tests are performed according to program requirements.
Testing includes enterprise and environmental reconnaissance for exploitable information.
Tests occur at least annually.
A qualified party with specialized skills and experience conducts the testing.

rows.title: Remediate Penetration Test Findings

rows: Penetration-test findings are remediated.
Remediation follows the documented vulnerability-remediation process.
Timelines are determined based on finding impact and prioritization.
Level of effort is determined based on finding impact and prioritization.

rows.title: Validate Security Measures

rows: Security measures are validated after each penetration test.
Rulesets and capabilities are modified to detect tested techniques if deemed necessary.

rows.title: Perform Periodic Internal Penetration Tests

rows: Internal penetration tests are performed.
Testing follows penetration-testing program requirements.
Internal tests occur at least annually.
